content:
Today we are excited to release Axiomatic Octo Search, bringing semantic search to any Lean project in just a few clicks.

Key Features

  • Search everywhere: Within minutes of pushing your code to GitHub, you can query all the declarations in your project along with its dependencies
  • Easy setup: Configure it easily via the wizard in our Octo VSCode extension to enable semantic search across every branch of your repository and its common dependencies.
  • Built for humans and non humans: Access Octo Search directly in VSCode, or integrate it with your favorite AI agent using our CLI and skills interface.

You can install the Octo VSCode extension to set up semantic search on your repo. Please don’t hesitate to reach out on Zuliip with feedback

We’re also preparing to release Octo Search open source, along with a GitHub Actions workflow template for users who prefer to run it themselves.

This is the first publicly released component of Octo, the (auto)formalization toolset we build and use internally at Axiomatic, with more releases to follow soon.

I want to thank the authors of LeanSearch v2, LeanExplore and doc-gen4. These projects have been hugely influential and when building Octo Search we drew heavily on their ideas. We used benchmarks proposed in the LeanSearch v2 paper to evaluate Octo Search. More details to follow in the technical report.
If you have any questions on the setup or anything else, here is the discussion thread: #general > Discussion thread for Octo Search .

Bumping this announcement since we are releasing a number of new features, after discussion with the first users who tried it (thank you very much to everyone!). Aside from some UI improvements, we now have:

Web-Search:

  1. You can now search any publicly listed repo on our brand new website, with no local install of anything.

  2. Dually, you can make your project searchable online by anyone! Of course you can also just continue to search your own repo privately locally, public listing is an optional opt-in. You can always decide to list it later, and if you have it listed you can de-list at any time from your dashboard.

  3. You can generate a unique shareable link that points to the search page toggled with just your repo and its dependencies. This way project contributors don't need to index their own forks if they don't want to, but can still easily search the project.

  4. You can provide links to your project landing page and documentation page, so that every declaration now links to its docs entry, as well as to the code on GitHub.

  5. You can have your agent query any publicly indexed repo via the MCP server.

Explanatory Manual:

  1. There is now a manual with more detailed instructions for customized setups.
